Remark 3.21
.

The technique of applying
subsection 3.1
in proving
subsection 3.2
will be used many times in the rest of the paper. Although the process is straightforward, individual details will vary from case to case, thus in order to simplify the process we will omit details in the future.

Recall
\gamma_{2}=k{\cdot}e+t
where
k
is a nonnegative integer and
2\leq t\leq e+1
. Now we remove the restriction on
\gamma_{2}
by applying the induction on
k
.

Proposition 3.22
.

Suppose
\gamma=(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2})\in\mathscr{C}_{n}^{\Lambda}
with
\gamma_{2}>1
and
\gamma_{2}-\gamma_{1}\equiv 1\pmod{e}
and
\lambda=(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2}-1,1)\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. Define
i
to be the residue of the node at position
(1,m,1)
. Then (
3.15
) holds.

Proof.

We prove this Proposition by induction. As we claimed before that we can write
\gamma_{2}=k{\cdot}e+t
with
2\leq t\leq e+1
and we will apply induction on
k
.
subsection 3.2
implies that for
k=0
the Proposition holds. Assume that for
k\leq k^{\prime}
the Proposition holds. For
k=k^{\prime}
, we consider two different cases, which are
i=e-2
,
i=e-1
and
i\neq e-2,e-1
. Recall that
i
is the residue of the node at
(1,m,1)
or
(2,m+1,1)
.

Case
3.2
a:

i\neq e-2,e-1
.

In both cases, the parts bounded by square are both
e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}
. As
|\sigma|=n-2
and
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, by induction,
e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}\in R^{>\sigma}_{n}
. By the definition of
\sigma
and
subsection 2.4
, it forces that
e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}\in R^{>\lambda|_{n-2}}_{n}
. Then by
subsection 3.1
, we have
e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. ∎

3.3. Final part of
y
-problem

In the last subsection we have proved that if
\lambda=(m,m,1)\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, then

e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}

with
k=i_{n}+1
. In this subsection we will gradually remove the restrictions on
\lambda
and
k
. First we are going to introduce a useful homomorphism and use it to prove a few more properties of
\mathscr{R}_{n}
and
\mathscr{R}^{\Lambda}_{n}
. After that we are going to show that if
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}_{I}^{\Lambda}
, then we can extend
\lambda
to a
\ell+1
multipartition by adding an
\emptyset
at the end and thus the new multipartition is in
\mathscr{P}_{I}^{\Lambda+\Lambda_{i}}
for any
i\in I
. Analogous results are also true for
\mathscr{P}_{y}^{\Lambda}
and
\mathscr{P}_{\psi}^{\Lambda}
. These will allow us to extend the result to an arbitrary multipartition
\lambda
.

For any
\mathbf{j}\in I^{m}
, we can define a linear map
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{j}}\,{:}\,\mathscr{R}_{n}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathscr{R}_{n+m}^{\Lambda}
sending
e(\mathbf{i})
to
e(\mathbf{j}\vee\mathbf{i})
,
y_{r}
to
y_{r+m}
and
\psi_{r}
to
\psi_{r+m}
. This map
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{j}}
works as embedding from
\mathscr{R}_{n}
to
\mathscr{R}_{n+m}
followed by the projection onto
\mathscr{R}_{n+m}^{\Lambda}
.

Lemma 3.30
.

For
\mathbf{j}\in I^{m}
, the map
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{j}}
is a homomorphism.

Proof.

The map is defined to be linear. Hence we only have to check the relations. Since the relations of
\mathscr{R}_{n}
and
\mathscr{R}_{n+m}^{\Lambda}
from
subsection 2.1
are independent of the value of
r
, we see that
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{j}}
is a homomorphism. ∎

It will be necessary to cut a multicomposition
\lambda
into one multicomposition
\mu
and a composition
\gamma
for our later work. Note that in our work we will mainly set
\mu
to be a multipartition and
\gamma
to be a partition, but generally we don’t have such restriction.

height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,\hskip 2.84526pt\Bigg|\hskip 2.84526pt\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,\hskip 2.84526pt\Bigg),

and a partition
\gamma
with diagram

[\gamma]=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,.

We call
\mu
and
\gamma
the cut part and the remaining part, respectively.

Moreover we want to preserve the following data. The value
|\mu|
is called the cut of
\lambda
which is 14 in this case. The residue of the top left node of
\gamma
as a subdiagram of
\lambda^{(3)}
is called the cut residue, which in this case is 3.

Now we give a formal definition.

Definition 3.32
.

Suppose
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})\in\mathscr{C}_{n}^{\Lambda}
with
\lambda^{(\ell)}=(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k_{\ell}})
and
a
is an integer such that
0\leq a<k_{\ell}
. We call
m
a
cut
of
\lambda
and
a
the
cut row
associated to
m
where
m=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell-1}|\lambda^{(i)}|+\sum_{j=1}^{a}\lambda_{j}^{(\ell)}
. Define
\Lambda^{\prime}=\Lambda_{s}
, where
s=\kappa_{\ell}+1-(a+1)=\kappa_{\ell}-a
, the residue of the node at position
(a+1,1,\ell)
. We call
s
to be
cut residue
associated to
m
and
\Lambda^{\prime}
to be
cut weight
associated to
m
. We then define
\mu=\lambda|_{m}\in\mathscr{C}^{\Lambda}_{m}
and
\gamma=(\lambda_{a+1}^{(\ell)},\lambda_{a+2}^{(\ell)},\ldots,\lambda_{k_{\ell}}^{(\ell)})\in\mathscr{C}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}_{n-m}
and call
\mu
and
\gamma
to be
cut part
and
remaining part
of
\lambda
associated to
m
, respectively.

Note we can either remove a portion of the last tableau, or cut out the whole partition.

We will start to work with
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}}
, which involving elements in both
\mathscr{R}_{n}
and
\mathscr{R}^{\Lambda}_{n}
. Recall that
\hat{e}(\mathbf{i})
,
\hat{y}_{r}
,
\hat{\psi}_{s}
and
\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}
are elements from
\mathscr{R}_{n}
and
e(\mathbf{i})
,
y_{r}
,
\psi_{s}
and
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}
are elements from
\mathscr{R}^{\Lambda}_{n}
.

Lemma 3.33
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. Let
m
be a cut of
\lambda
with
m<n-1
,
\nu=\lambda|_{m}
and
\Lambda^{\prime}
be the cut weight associated to
m
. Consider
N_{n-m}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}\subseteq\mathscr{R}_{n-m}
. If
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}\,{:}\,\mathscr{R}_{n-m}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathscr{R}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, then
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(N_{n-m}^{\Lambda^{\prime}})y_{\nu}\subseteq R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

Proof.

Consider
r\in N_{n-m}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
. Then by (
2.40
),

r=\sum_{\mathbf{j}=(j_{1},j_{2},\ldots,j_{n-m})\in I^{n-m}}c_{\mathbf{j}}R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}}\hat{e}(\mathbf{j})\hat{y}_{1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}R_{\mathbf{j}},

where
R_{\mathbf{j}}
and
R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}}
are some elements in
\mathscr{R}_{n-m}
and
c_{\mathbf{j}}\in\mathbb{Z}
. Therefore

\displaystyle\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(r)y_{\nu}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{j}=(j_{1},j_{2},\ldots,j_{n-m})\in I^{n-m}}c_{\mathbf{j}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(\hat{e}(\mathbf{j})\hat{y}_{1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R_{\mathbf{j}})y_{\nu}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{j}=(j_{1},j_{2},\ldots,j_{n-m})\in I^{n-m}}c_{\mathbf{j}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}})e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee j_{1}\vee j_{2}j_{3}\ldots j_{n-m})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R_{\mathbf{j}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{j}=(j_{1},j_{2},\ldots,j_{n-m})\in I^{n-m}}c_{\mathbf{j}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}})\theta_{(j_{2},j_{3},\ldots,j_{n-m})}(e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee j_{1})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R_{\mathbf{j}}).

Next we consider
e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee j_{1})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}\in\mathscr{R}_{m+1}^{\Lambda}
.

Recall that we can write
\nu=(\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)},\nu^{(\ell)})
and
\nu^{(\ell)}=(\nu^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\nu^{(\ell)}_{l})
. Let
\mu=\lambda|_{m+1}
. As
m<n-1
,
|\mu|=m+1<n=|\lambda|
, and
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, we have
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
. Write
\mathbf{i}_{\nu}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{m})
. Notice that
(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})=|\mathscr{A}_{\mathsf{t}^{\nu}}^{j_{1}}|
. We consider two cases.

Suppose
{j_{1}}=i_{m}+1
and
\nu^{+}
is a multipartition. By
subsection 3.1
we have
|\mathscr{A}_{\mathsf{t}^{\nu}}^{j_{1}}|=b_{j_{1}}^{\nu}-1
. Then by
subsection 3.1
we have
e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{b_{j_{1}}^{\nu}-1}=e_{\nu^{+}}y_{\nu^{+}}
. Because
m
is a cut of
\lambda
and
\nu=\lambda|_{m}
,
\mu=\lambda|_{m+1}
, we must have
\nu^{+}>\mu
. Therefore
e_{\nu^{+}}y_{\nu^{+}}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}
. So

e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}.

Otherwise, by
subsection 3.1
we have
|\mathscr{A}_{\mathsf{t}^{\nu}}^{j_{1}}|=b_{j_{1}}^{\nu}
. Then by
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
and the definition of
\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
, for any
{j_{1}}\in I
, we have
e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{b_{j_{1}}^{\nu}}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}
because
\nu=\mu_{-}
. Therefore

e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{b_{j_{1}}^{\nu}}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}.

Therefore for any
{j_{1}}\in I
we have
e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee{j_{1}})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}
. Hence by
subsection 3.1
and
subsection 3.1
,

\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}})\theta_{(j_{2},j_{3},\ldots,j_{n-m})}(e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee j_{1})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R_{\mathbf{j}})\subseteq R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

Therefore
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(r)y_{\nu}=\sum_{\mathbf{j}=(j_{1},j_{2},\ldots,j_{n-m})\in I^{n-m}}c_{\mathbf{j}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R^{\prime}_{\mathbf{j}})\theta_{(j_{2},j_{3},\ldots,j_{n-m})}(e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu}\vee j_{1})y_{\nu}y_{m+1}^{(\Lambda^{\prime},\alpha_{j_{1}})})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu}}(R_{\mathbf{j}})\subseteq R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.
∎

Definition 3.34
.

Suppose
\lambda
is a multicomposition of
m
and
\mu
is a composition. If there exists a multicomposition
\gamma
such that
\lambda
and
\mu
are cut part and remaining part of
\gamma
associated
m
, we write
\gamma=\lambda\vee\mu
and say
\gamma
is the
concatenation
of
\lambda
and
\mu
.

For example, suppose
\lambda=(2^{2},1|3^{3}|2)
and
\mu=(4,2)
, then
\gamma=\lambda\vee\mu=(2^{2},1|3^{3}|2,4,2)
. Notice that in general
\gamma
is not a multipartition.

The following Corollaries follows by the definition of
\lambda\vee\mu
.

Corollary 3.35
.

Suppose
\lambda
is a multipartition of
n
and
\mu,\gamma
are partitions of
m
. Then
\mu>\gamma
if and only if
\lambda\vee\mu>\lambda\vee\gamma
.

Corollary 3.36
.

Suppose
\lambda
is a multipartition of
n
and
\mu
is a partition of
m
. If
\gamma=\lambda\vee\mu
,
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\lambda}}(\hat{e}_{\mu}\hat{y}_{\mu})y_{\lambda}=e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}
.

Corollary 3.37
.

Suppose
\lambda
and
\mu
are multipartitions and
\gamma
is a partition such that
\lambda=\mu\vee\gamma
. If
\mathsf{u}
and
\mathsf{v}
are standard
\gamma
-tableaux, there exist standard
\lambda
-tableaux
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
and
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
such that
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}=\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}
.

Proof.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
and
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{m}
. By
subsection 3.3
,
\mu
is the cut part of
\lambda
associated to
m
. Let
a
be the cut row associated to
m
. Define
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
to be the standard
\lambda
-tableau such that
\dot{\mathsf{u}}|_{m}=\mathsf{t}^{\mu}
, and for any
k>m
, if
\dot{\mathsf{u}}^{-1}(k)=(r_{1},c_{1},\ell_{1})
and
\mathsf{u}^{-1}(k-m)=(r_{2},c_{2},1)
, then

\begin{array}[]{rl}&c_{1}=c_{2},\\
&r_{1}=r_{2}+a.\end{array}

Define
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
similarly. It is trivial that
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{u})})=\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}
and
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{v})})=\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}
. Therefore by
subsection 3.3
,

\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{u})}^{*})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{e}_{\gamma}\hat{y}_{\gamma})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{v})})=\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}.

∎

Lemma 3.38
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\mu\in\mathscr{C}_{n}^{\Lambda}
with
\mu>\lambda
. If
\mu_{-}\neq\lambda_{-}
, then
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

Proof.

As
\mu>\lambda
and
\mu_{-}\neq\lambda_{-}
, there exists
m<n
such that
\mu|_{m}>\lambda|_{m}
and
\mu|_{m-1}=\lambda|_{m-1}
. Set
\nu=\mu|_{m}
. If
\nu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{m}
, we have
e_{\nu}y_{\nu}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\nu}\mathsf{t}^{\nu}}\in R^{>\lambda|_{m}}_{n}
, so by
subsection 3.1
we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

If
\nu\not\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{m}
, because
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
|\nu|=m<n
, we have
\nu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
. Notice that if we write
\nu=(\nu^{(1)},\ldots,\nu^{(l)},\emptyset,\ldots,\emptyset)
with
\nu^{(l)}=(\nu^{(l)}_{1},\ldots,\nu^{(l)}_{k-1},\nu^{(l)}_{k})
, because
\nu|_{m-1}=\mu|_{m-1}=\lambda|_{m-1}\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{m-1}
and
\nu\not\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{m}
, we must have
\nu_{k-1}^{(l)}+1=\nu_{k}^{(l)}
. Therefore if we write
\mathbf{i}_{\nu}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{m})
, we have

e_{\nu}y_{\nu}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\nu_{-}}\vee i_{m})y_{\nu_{-}}y_{m}^{b_{i_{m}}^{\nu_{-}}}\in R^{>\nu}_{n}\subseteq R^{>\lambda|_{m}}_{n}.

Then by
subsection 3.1
, we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. This completes the proof. ∎

Now we are ready to start proving the main result of this section. We start by proving two more specialized Propositions. After that we will introduce a Proposition which removes these restrictions and leads to the main Theorem of this section.

Proposition 3.39
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\lambda_{-}=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{-})
with
\lambda^{(\ell)}_{-}=(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-1},\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l})\neq\emptyset
. Write
\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{n-1})
. For
k\in I
, if
k\neq i_{n-1}+1
, or
k=i_{n-1}+1
and
\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-1}>\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l}
, we have

e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

Proof.

For convenience set
m=\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l}
and
\mu=\lambda|_{n-m-1}
. Therefore
\mu=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)},\mu^{(\ell)})
where

\mu^{(\ell)}=\begin{cases}(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-1}),&\text{ if $l>1$,}\\
\emptyset,&\text{ if $l=1$.}\end{cases}

Suppose
i
is the residue of node
(l,1,\ell)
in
\lambda
and
\Lambda^{\prime}=\Lambda_{i}
. Define
\gamma=(m+1)\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}_{m+1}
. Notice that
\lambda_{-}=\mu\vee\gamma_{-}
. Because
k\neq i_{n-1}+1
or
k=i_{n-1}+1
and
\lambda_{k-1}^{(\ell)}>\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)}
, we have
b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}=b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}
. By
subsection 3.1
, in
\mathscr{R}_{m+1}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
we have
e(\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)y_{\gamma_{-}}y_{m+1}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}}\in R^{>\gamma}_{n}
. This implies that in
\mathscr{R}_{m+1}
,
\hat{e}(\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)\hat{y}_{\gamma_{-}}\hat{y}_{m+1}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}}\in N_{m+1}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
. Then let
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}\,{:}\,\mathscr{R}_{m+1}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathscr{R}^{\Lambda}_{n}
, by
subsection 3.3
,

e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu}\vee\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{e}(\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)\hat{y}_{\gamma_{-}}\hat{y}_{m+1}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}})y_{\mu}\in\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(N_{m+1}^{\Lambda^{\prime}})y_{\mu}\subseteq R^{>\lambda}_{n},

which completes the proof.∎

Proposition 3.40
.

Suppose
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
with
\lambda^{(\ell)}=(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-1},\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l},1)
and
l\geq 2
, where
\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-1}=\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l}
. Write
\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{n-1})
. Suppose
k\in I
and
k\equiv i_{n-1}+1\pmod{e}
. Then

e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

Proof.

For convenience set
m=\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-1}=\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l}
, and
\mu=\lambda|_{n-2m-1}
. Therefore
\mu=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)},\mu^{(\ell)})
where

\mu^{(\ell)}=\begin{cases}(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{l-2}),&\text{ if $l>2$,}\\
\emptyset,&\text{ if $l=2$.}\end{cases}

Suppose
i
is the residue of node
(l-1,1,\ell)
in
\lambda
and
\Lambda^{\prime}=\Lambda_{i}
. Define
\gamma=(m,m+1)\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}_{2m+1}
. Notice that
\lambda_{-}=\mu\vee\gamma_{-}
. Because
k\equiv i_{n-1}+1\pmod{e}
, we have
b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}=b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}
and
e(\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)y_{\gamma_{-}}y_{2m+1}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}}=e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}
. By
subsection 3.2
, we have
e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\in R^{>\gamma}_{n}
. Therefore we can write
e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\sigma)\\
\sigma>\gamma\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}
with
\sigma=(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})
where
\sigma_{2}\geq 0
and
\sigma_{1}>\gamma_{1}=m
. Therefore in
\mathscr{R}_{2m+1}
, we have

\hat{e}_{\gamma}\hat{y}_{\gamma}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\sigma)\\
\sigma>\gamma\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}+r,

with
r\in N_{2m+1}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
and
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\in\mathbb{Z}
. Therefore

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}

\displaystyle=e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu}\vee\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{e}(\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)\hat{y}_{\gamma_{-}}\hat{y}_{2m+1}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}})y_{\mu}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{e}_{\gamma}\hat{y}_{\gamma})y_{\mu}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\sigma)\\
\sigma>\gamma\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}+\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(r).

(3.41)

For the first term of (
3.41
), define
\alpha=\mu\vee\sigma\in\mathscr{C}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. Because
\sigma>\gamma
, by
subsection 3.3
we have
\alpha=\mu\vee\sigma>\mu\vee\gamma>\lambda
. Therefore

\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{u})}^{*})\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{e}_{\sigma}\hat{y}_{\sigma})y_{\mu}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{v})})=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{u})}^{*})e_{\mu\vee\sigma}y_{\mu\vee\sigma}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{v})})=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{u})}^{*})e_{\alpha}y_{\alpha}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{v})})

Because
\sigma=(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})>\gamma=(m,m+1)
, we must have
\sigma_{1}>m
. Therefore
\alpha_{-}=\mu\vee\sigma_{-}\neq\mu\vee\gamma_{-}=\lambda_{-}
. Then by
subsection 3.3
,
e_{\alpha}y_{\alpha}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. By
subsection 3.1
, we have
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{u})}^{*})e_{\alpha}y_{\alpha}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{d(\mathsf{v})})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
which yields
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\sigma)\\
\sigma>\gamma\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

For the second term of (
3.41
), by
subsection 3.3
, we have
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(r)\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Therefore

e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

∎

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. If
\lambda_{-}=(\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)},\lambda_{-}^{(\ell)})
with
\lambda_{-}^{(\ell)}\neq\emptyset
by
subsection 3.3
and
subsection 3.3
we have
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
. In the rest of the subsection we are going to prove the result is still true if
\lambda_{-}^{(\ell)}=\emptyset
.

Suppose
\mu=(\mu^{(1)},\ldots,\mu^{(\ell)})\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
and
\kappa_{\Lambda}=(\kappa_{1},\ldots,\kappa_{\ell})
, if
\mu^{(\ell)}=\emptyset
, we define
\bar{\Lambda}=\Lambda-\Lambda_{\kappa_{\ell}}
,
\kappa_{\bar{\Lambda}}=(\kappa_{1},\ldots,\kappa_{\ell-1})
and
\bar{\mu}=(\mu^{(1)},\ldots,\mu^{(\ell-1)})\in\mathscr{P}^{\bar{\Lambda}}_{n}
. Suppose
\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}
are two standard
\mu
-tableaux, define
\bar{\mathsf{u}}
and
\bar{\mathsf{v}}
to be standard
\bar{\mu}
-tableaux obtained by removing the
\emptyset
at the end of
\mathsf{u}
and
\mathsf{v}
respectively. Write
k=\kappa_{\ell}
for convenience. If
\mathbf{i}=(i_{1},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n}
, define

y_{\mathbf{i},k}=y_{1}^{\delta_{i_{1},k}}y_{2}^{\delta_{i_{2},k}}\ldots y_{n}^{\delta_{i_{n},k}}.

Lemma 3.42
.

Suppose the notations are defined as above and
\mathbf{i}_{\mathsf{v}}
is the residue sequence of
\mathsf{v}
, then

\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}=\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\nu},k},

where
\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}
is an element in
\mathscr{R}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}
is an element in
\mathscr{R}_{n}^{\bar{\Lambda}}
.

Proof.

Without loss of generality, assume
\mathsf{u}=\mathsf{t}^{\mu}
. By the definition of
\mu
and
\bar{\mu}
, writing
\mathbf{i}_{\mu}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{n})
, we have
y_{\mu}=y_{\bar{\mu}}y_{1}^{\delta_{i_{1},k}}y_{2}^{\delta_{i_{2},k}}\ldots y_{n}^{\delta_{i_{n},k}}=y_{\bar{\mu}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu},k}
.

Now for any residue sequence
\mathbf{i}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{n})\in I^{n}
and any
r
, If
i_{r}\neq i_{r+1}

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i})y_{1}^{\delta_{i_{1},k}}y_{2}^{\delta_{i_{2},k}}\ldots y_{n}^{\delta_{i_{n},k}}\psi_{r}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle(e(\mathbf{i})y_{r}^{\delta_{i_{r},k}}y_{r+1}^{\delta_{i_{r+1},k}}\psi_{r})y_{1}^{\delta_{i_{1},k}}\ldots y_{r-1}^{\delta_{i_{r-1},k}}y_{r+2}^{\delta_{i_{r+1},k}}\ldots y_{n}^{\delta_{i_{n},k}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i})\psi_{r}y_{r}^{\delta_{i_{r+1},k}}y_{r+1}^{\delta_{i_{r},k}}y_{1}^{\delta_{i_{1},k}}\ldots y_{r-1}^{\delta_{i_{r-1},k}}y_{r+2}^{\delta_{i_{r+1},k}}\ldots y_{n}^{\delta_{i_{n},k}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i})\psi_{r}y_{1}^{\delta_{s_{r}(i_{1}),k}}\ldots y_{n}^{\delta_{s_{r}(i_{n}),k}}=e(\mathbf{i})\psi_{r}y_{\mathbf{i}{\cdot}s_{r},k}.

If
i_{r}=i_{r+1}
, then by relation (
2.13
), as
\delta_{i_{r},k}=\delta_{i_{r+1},k}
, we have the same result.

Hence

\displaystyle\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\mathsf{v}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{d(\mathsf{v})}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu})y_{\bar{\mu}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu},k}\psi_{d(\mathsf{v})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu})y_{\bar{\mu}}\psi_{d(\mathsf{v})}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}{\cdot}d(\mathsf{v}),k}=e_{\mu}y_{\bar{\mu}}\psi_{d(v)}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mathsf{v}},k}.

As
e_{\mu}=e_{\bar{\mu}}
and
\psi_{d(\mathsf{v})}=\psi_{d(\bar{\mathsf{v}})}
, this completes the proof. ∎

Proposition 3.43
.

Suppose
\mu
,
\kappa_{\Lambda}
,
\bar{\mu}
, and
\kappa_{\bar{\Lambda}}
are defined as above. Then
\bar{\mu}\in\mathscr{P}_{I}^{\bar{\Lambda}}\cap\mathscr{P}_{y}^{\bar{\Lambda}}\cap\mathscr{P}_{\psi}^{\bar{\Lambda}}
implies
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi}
.

Proof.

We are only going to prove that
\bar{\mu}\in\mathscr{P}_{I}^{\bar{\Lambda}}
implies
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
. The other two cases are similar.

Suppose
\bar{\mu}\in\mathscr{P}^{\bar{\Lambda}}_{I}
. Then for any
s\in I
, by the definition of
\mathscr{P}^{\bar{\Lambda}}_{I}
,

e(\mathbf{i}_{\bar{\mu}_{-}}\vee s)y_{\bar{\mu}_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}=\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}},

where
\mathbf{i}_{\bar{\mathsf{v}}}=\mathbf{i}_{\bar{\mu}_{-}}\vee s=\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s
and
c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Also we have
e(\mathbf{i}_{\bar{\mu}_{-}}\vee s)y_{\bar{\mu}_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}=\theta_{s}(\psi_{t^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}t^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}
. Therefore we have

\theta_{s}(\psi_{t^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}t^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}=\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}.

Notice that
\mathsf{t}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}=\overline{\mathsf{t}^{\mu_{-}}}
. Recall
k=\kappa_{\ell}
, the last term of the multicharge
\kappa_{\Lambda}
. We consider two cases,
s\neq k
and
s=k
in the rest of the proof.

If
s\neq k
, then
b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}=b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}
. Hence by
subsection 3.3

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s)y_{\mu_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{s}(\psi_{t^{\mu_{-}}t^{\mu_{-}}})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{s}(\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{t}}^{\mu_{-}}\bar{\mathsf{t}}^{\mu_{-}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{s}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}\mathsf{t}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k},

and as
s\neq k
,
\delta_{s,k}=0
. Hence
y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k}=y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s,k}=y_{\mathbf{i}_{\bar{\mathsf{v}}},k}=y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mathsf{v}},k}
. By
subsection 3.3
,

e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s)y_{\mu_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}}=\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mathsf{v}},k}=\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n},

because
\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})
implies
\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\Std(>\mu)
.

If
s=k
, then
b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}=b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}+1
. Hence by
subsection 3.3

\displaystyle e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s)y_{\mu_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{s}(\psi_{t^{\mu_{-}}t^{\mu_{-}}})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{s}(\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{t}}^{\mu_{-}}\bar{\mathsf{t}}^{\mu_{-}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}y_{n}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{s}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}\mathsf{t}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}})y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\bar{\mu}_{-}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k}y_{n}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k}y_{n},

and as
s=k
,
\delta_{s,k}=1
. Hence
y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}},k}y_{n}=y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s,k}=y_{\mathbf{i}_{\bar{\mathsf{v}}},k}=y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mathsf{v}},k}
. By
subsection 3.3

e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee s)y_{\mu_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{s}^{\mu_{-}}}=\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}y_{\mathbf{i}_{\mathsf{v}},k}=\sum_{\bar{\mathsf{u}},\bar{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\bar{\mu})}c_{\bar{\mathsf{u}}\bar{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

These implies that
\mu\in\mathscr{P}_{I}
. ∎

Now we are ready to prove
subsection 3.1
.

Proof of
subsection 3.1
.
Write
\mu=\lambda_{-}=(\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)},\mu^{(\ell)})
. If
\mu^{(\ell)}\neq\emptyset
, by
subsection 3.3
and
subsection 3.3
, we have
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
.

If
\mu^{(\ell)}=\emptyset
, write
\lambda^{(\ell-1)}=(\lambda^{(\ell-1)}_{1},\lambda^{(\ell-1)}_{2},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)}_{k_{\ell-1}})
and define
\gamma=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-2)},\gamma^{(\ell-1)},\emptyset)\in\mathscr{P}_{n}^{\Lambda}
with
\gamma^{(\ell-1)}=(\lambda^{(\ell-1)}_{1},\lambda^{(\ell-1)}_{2},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)}_{k_{\ell-1}},1)
and
\bar{\gamma}=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-2)},\gamma^{(\ell-1)})
. As
l(\bar{\gamma})<l(\lambda)=\ell
, by the definition of
\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
,
\bar{\gamma}\in\mathscr{P}_{I}^{\bar{\Lambda}}
. Then by
subsection 3.3
we have
\gamma\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
. Since
\gamma_{-}=\mu=\lambda_{-}
and
\gamma>\lambda
, for any
k\in I
,

e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee k)y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\lambda_{-}}}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\gamma_{-}}\vee k)y_{\gamma_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{k}^{\gamma_{-}}}\in R^{>\gamma}_{n}\subseteq R^{>\lambda}_{n},

which yields that
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}_{I}
. This completes the proof.

The following Corollary is directly implied by
subsection 3.1
. It will contribute to proving the
\psi
-problem.

Corollary 3.44
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\mu\in\mathscr{C}_{n}^{\Lambda}
where
\mu>\lambda
. Then we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

Proof.

If
\mu_{-}\neq\lambda_{-}
, using
subsection 3.3
we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Suppose then that
\mu_{-}=\lambda_{-}
. If
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
, then
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Finally, suppose that
\mu\not\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
. If we write
\mu=(\mu^{(1)},\ldots,\mu^{(l)},\emptyset,\ldots,\emptyset)
with
\mu^{(l)}=(\mu^{(l)}_{1},\ldots,\mu^{(l)}_{k-1},\mu^{(l)}_{k})
, we must have
\mu^{(l)}_{k-1}+1=\mu^{(l)}_{k}
. If we write
\mathbf{i}_{\mu}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{n})
, we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\mu_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{i_{n}}^{\mu_{-}}}
. By
subsection 3.1
, as
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, we have
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}
. Since
\lambda_{-}=\mu_{-}
,

e_{\mu}y_{\mu}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\mu_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{i_{n}}^{\mu_{-}}}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{i_{n}}^{\lambda_{-}}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

∎

4. Integral Basis Theorem II

In this section our main purpose is to prove that
\mathscr{R}^{\Lambda}_{n}=R^{\Lambda}_{n}
by proving that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}
and
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}
are both in
R^{\Lambda}_{n}
. We first define an integer
m_{\lambda}
such that if
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
, we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\Lambda}_{n}
and
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\Lambda}_{n}
. Our first step is to show that
m_{\lambda}>0
. Then we prove if
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, we will have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\Lambda}_{n}
and
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\Lambda}_{n}
as well. By induction we will show that for any
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
,
l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
, which indicates that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\Lambda}_{n}
and
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\Lambda}_{n}
for any
\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
. Finally combining the results from the last section, we can prove that
\mathscr{R}^{\Lambda}_{n}=R^{\Lambda}_{n}
.

4.1. Base case of induction

In this section we fix
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. First we will give a proper definition of
m_{\lambda}
.

Definition 4.1
.

Define
m_{\lambda}
to be the smallest nonnegative integer such that for any standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{t}
with
l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
we have

\displaystyle\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},

\displaystyle\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}+\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{w}=\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}$ is standard and $d(\mathsf{u}){\cdot}s_{r}$ is reduced,}\\
\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{u}{\cdot}s_{r}$ is not standard or $d(\mathsf{u}){\cdot}s_{r}$ is not reduced.}\end{cases}

for some
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\in\mathbb{Z}
.

We will use induction to prove that for any
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
,
l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
in this section. In this subsection we will prove that
m_{\lambda}>0
, which is the base case of the induction.

Lemma 4.2
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. For any
1\leq r\leq n
,
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}y_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}}y_{r}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

Proof.

If
r<n
, write
\mu=\lambda|_{r}
. As
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
we have
\mu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}
. Therefore
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}y_{r}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}
. By
subsection 3.1
, we have
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}y_{r}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

If
r=n
, write
\mathbf{i}_{\lambda}=(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{n})
. There exists a positive integer
b
such that
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b}
. By the definition of
b_{i_{n}}^{\lambda_{-}}
we have
b<b_{i_{n}}^{\lambda_{-}}
. If
b+1<b_{i_{n}}^{\lambda_{-}}
, by
subsection 3.1
there exists
\nu\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
such that

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}y_{n}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b+1}=e_{\nu}y_{\nu},

and it is trivial that
\nu>\lambda
. Therefore
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}y_{n}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. If we have
b+1=b_{i_{n}}^{\lambda_{-}}
, by
subsection 3.1
we have

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}y_{n}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b+1}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda_{-}}\vee i_{n})y_{\lambda_{-}}y_{n}^{b_{i_{n}}^{\lambda_{-}}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n},

which completes the proof. ∎

Lemma 4.3
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. For any
1\leq r<n
,
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Proof.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r}=\mathsf{t}
is standard, we have
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. So we consider the case that
\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r}=\mathsf{t}
is not standard. If
r<n-1
, as
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, we have
\mu=\lambda_{-}\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi}
. Because
\mathsf{t}^{\mu}{\cdot}s_{r}=\mathsf{t}|_{n-1}
which is not standard,
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{r}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}
. Then by
subsection 3.1
, we have
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. If
r=n-1
and write
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(l)},\emptyset,\ldots,\emptyset)
with
\lambda^{(l)}=(\lambda^{(l)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(l)}_{k-1},\lambda^{(l)}_{k})
, we must have either
\lambda^{(l)}_{k}\geq 2
or
\lambda^{(l)}_{k-1}=\lambda^{(l)}_{k}=1
. Then set
\mu=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\mu^{(l)},\emptyset,\ldots,\emptyset)
with

\mu^{(l)}=\begin{cases}(\lambda^{(l)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(l)}_{k-1}),&\text{ if $\lambda^{(l)}_{k}\geq 2$ and $k>1$,}\\
(\lambda^{(l)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(l)}_{k-2}),&\text{ if $\lambda^{(l)}_{k-1}=\lambda^{(l)}_{k}=1$ and $k>2$,}\\
\emptyset,&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

Suppose
i
is the residue of node
(k,1,l)
in
\lambda
or the residue of node
(k-1,1,l)
in
\lambda
,
\Lambda^{\prime}=\Lambda_{i}
,
m=\lambda^{(l)}_{k}
or
m=2
and
\gamma=(m)\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}_{m}
or
\gamma=(1,1)\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}_{m}
if
\lambda^{(l)}_{k}\geq 2
or
\lambda^{(l)}_{k-1}=\lambda^{(l)}_{k}=1
respectively. Therefore
\lambda=\mu\vee\gamma
. Because
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, we have
\gamma\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi}
. Hence because
\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}{\cdot}s_{m-1}
is not standard, we have
e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{m-1}\in R^{>\gamma}_{n}=N_{m}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
. Then by
subsection 3.3
,

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r}=e(\mathbf{i}_{\mu}\vee\mathbf{i}_{\gamma})y_{\lambda}\psi_{r}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{m-1})y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n},

which completes the proof. ∎

Corollary 4.4
.

For
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, we have
m_{\lambda}>0
.

Proof.

Combining the above two Lemmas,
subsection 2.4
and
subsection 2.4
, the Corollary follows.∎

4.2. Completion of the
y
-problem

In this subsection we are going to prove that for any
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
, if
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, then for any
1\leq r\leq n-1
and any
\mathsf{s}\in\Std(\lambda)
, if
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced,
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
and for any
1\leq r\leq n
,
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

First we introduce the following Lemma.

Lemma 4.5
.

Suppose
m
is a positive integer such that
m\leq m_{\lambda}
, then

\displaystyle e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}

\displaystyle=_{\lambda}

\displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\text{Std}(\lambda)\\
l(d(\mathsf{v}))\leq m\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{t^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}.

Proof.

We apply induction on
m
. Suppose
m=0
then there is nothing to prove. Assume for any
m^{\prime}<m
the Lemma holds. Therefore
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m-1}}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u}\in\text{Std}(\lambda)\\
l(d(\mathsf{u}))\leq m-1\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{t^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}
which yields

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m-1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u}\in\text{Std}(\lambda)\\
l(d(\mathsf{u}))\leq m-1\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{t^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{r_{m}}.

For
\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\lambda)
and
l(d(\mathsf{u}))\leq m-1<m_{\lambda}
, if
\mathsf{u}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
s_{d(\mathsf{v})}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}
is reduced, by the definition of
m_{\lambda}
,

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{u}{\cdot}s_{r}}+\sum_{(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{u})}c_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}\psi_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}=_{\lambda}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{u}{\cdot}s_{r}}+\sum_{\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{u}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}},

where
l(d(\mathsf{u}{\cdot}s_{r}))=1+l(d(\mathsf{u}))\leq m
and
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{u}))<m
as
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{u}
. Hence

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{r_{m}}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\text{Std}(\lambda)\\
l(d(\mathsf{v}))\leq m\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{v}}\psi_{t^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}.

If
\mathsf{u}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
s_{d(\mathsf{v})}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}
is not reduced, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{(\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{u})}c_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}\psi_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{u}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}},

where
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{u}))\leq m-1<m
as
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{u}
. Hence

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{u}}\psi_{r_{m}}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\text{Std}(\lambda)\\
l(d(\mathsf{v}))\leq m\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{t^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}},

which completes the proof. ∎

Now we can start to prove that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
when
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced.

Lemma 4.6
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau with
d(\mathsf{t})=s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l}}
where
l\leq m_{\lambda}
, and
d^{\prime}(t)=s_{t_{1}}s_{t_{2}}\ldots s_{t_{l}}
is another reduced decomposition of
d(\mathsf{t})
, then

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}-e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d^{\prime}(\mathsf{t})}=\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Proof.

By
[
5
, Proposition 2.5]
, we have

y_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}-y_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}\psi_{d^{\prime}(\mathsf{t})}=\sum_{u<d(\mathsf{t})}c_{u,f}y_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}f(y)\psi_{u},

where
f(y)
is a polynomial in
y_{r}
’s and
u
is a word in
\mathfrak{S}_{n}
. If
f(y)\neq 1
, by
subsection 4.1
we have
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}f(y)\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Hence
y_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}f(y)\psi_{u}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. If
f(y)=1
, as
u<d(\mathsf{t})
then
l(u)<l\leq m_{\lambda}
, by
subsection 4.2
we have
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{u}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. Henceforth

y_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}\psi_{w}-y_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}\psi_{w^{\prime}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

Then by
subsection 2.4
and
[
9
, Lemma 5.7]
, we complete the proof.∎

The following Corollary is straightforward by
subsection 4.2
which explains the action of
\psi_{r}
to
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}
from right when
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced.

Corollary 4.7
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau with
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, if
\mathsf{w}=\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced,

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}+\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Now we start to prove that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Lemma 4.8
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau with
l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
. For any
1\leq k\leq n
,
1\leq r\leq n-1
and any standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{s}
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{k}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

Proof.

As
l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{k}=\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}=\sum_{\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

For
\Shape(\mathsf{v})=\lambda
, since
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}
,
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{t}))<m_{\lambda}
. Then we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

For
\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\lambda)
,
\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. As
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
,
R^{>\lambda}_{n}
is an ideal by
subsection 3.1
. Hence
\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r_{l}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
and this completes the proof. ∎

Proposition 4.9
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau with
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, for any
1\leq r\leq n
and any standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{s}
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}=\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Proof.

Write
d(\mathsf{t})=s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-1}}s_{r_{l}}
and
\mathsf{w}=\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r_{l}}=s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-1}}
. We prove this Proposition by considering different values of
r
.

If
r\not\in\{r_{l},r_{l}+1\}
, then
\psi_{r_{l}}
and
y_{r}
commute. Hence

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}=\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}y_{r}=\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}y_{r}\psi_{r_{l}}=\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}y_{r}\psi_{r_{l}}.

As
l(d(\mathsf{w}))=l(d(\mathsf{t}))-1<m_{\lambda}
, by
subsection 4.2
we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

If
r=r_{l}
, let
\mathbf{j}
be a sequence such that
e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda})\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}=\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}e(\mathbf{j})\psi_{r_{l}}
. We separate this case further into
j_{r_{l}}\neq j_{r_{l}+1}
and
j_{r_{l}}=j_{r_{l}+1}
. First suppose
j_{r_{l}}\neq j_{r_{l}+1}
, then

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}=\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}y_{r}=\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}y_{r+1}\psi_{r_{l}}=\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}y_{r+1}\psi_{r_{l}}.

Hence as
l(d(\mathsf{w}))<m_{\lambda}
, by
subsection 4.2
we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
when
j_{r_{l}}\neq j_{r_{l}+1}
. Now suppose
j_{r_{l}}=j_{r_{l}+1}
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}=\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}\mathsf{y}_{r}=\psi^{*}_{d(\mathsf{s})}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}+\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}y_{r+1}\psi_{r_{l}}=\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}+\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}y_{r+1}\psi_{r_{l}}.

As
l(d(\mathsf{w}))<m_{\lambda}
, by
subsection 4.2
we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}y_{r+1}\psi_{r_{l}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. As
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
as well, we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. So for
r=r_{l}
, we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

If
r=r_{l}+1
, the method is the same as
r=r_{l}
.

Therefore in all the cases, we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. So

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}y_{r}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\geq\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},

and by
subsection 2.4
we complete the proof.∎

4.3. Properties of
m_{\lambda}

In the rest of this section we will prove that if
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, then for any
1\leq r\leq n-1
and any
\mathsf{s}\in\Std(\lambda)
, we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. In this subsection we will give some properties for
m_{\lambda}
which will be used in proving the above argument.

Lemma 4.10
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
. For any permutation
w\in\mathfrak{S}_{n}
with reduced expression
w=s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{m-1}}s_{r_{m}}
and
r=\text{min}\{r_{1},r_{2},\ldots,r_{m}\}
, if we write

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{w}=e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\geq\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},

then
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\neq 0
implies
\mathsf{v}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for any
k<r
.

Proof.

We prove the Lemma by induction. If
m=1
, then
r_{1}=r
.

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r}=\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r}$ is standard,}\\
\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{t}^{\lambda})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

If
\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard, then by the definition of
\mathsf{v}
,
\mathsf{v}|_{k}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}|_{k}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for
k<r
. If it is the other case, as
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}
, then
\mathsf{v}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}|_{k}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
.

Assume for any
m^{\prime}<m
the Corollary holds. Then

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m-1}}=\sum_{\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1}\in\Std(\geq\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}},

where
\mathsf{v}_{1}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for
k<r
. Then

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m-1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1}\in\Std(\geq\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}.

Since

\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}_{2})\rhd(\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}_{2}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is standard and $d(\mathsf{v}_{1}){\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is reduced,}\\
\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

If
\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{v}_{1}){\cdot}s_{r_{m}}
is reduced, recall
\mathsf{v}_{1}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for
k<r
, as
\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}
,
\mathsf{v}|_{k}=\mathsf{v}_{1}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for
k<r\leq r_{m}
. For
\mathsf{v}_{2}\rhd\mathsf{v}_{1}
, we have
\mathsf{v}_{2}|_{k}\rhd\mathsf{v}_{1}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for
k<r
.

If it is of the other case, as
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{v}_{1}
,
\mathsf{v}|_{k}\rhd\mathsf{v}_{1}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
. Therefore

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{w}=e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\geq\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},

and
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\neq 0
implies
\mathsf{v}|_{k}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{k}}
for any
k<r
. This completes the proof. ∎

Lemma 4.11
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}\cap(\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi})
. Then for any
1\leq r_{1},r_{2},\ldots,r_{m}\leq n-1

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\lambda)\\
\mathsf{u}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Proof.

When
m=1
, we have

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}=\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r_{1}}$ is standard,}\\
\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{t}^{\lambda})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\lambda)\\
\mathsf{u}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r_{1}}$ is not standard.}\end{cases}

which follows the Lemma.

Suppose for
m^{\prime}<m
the Lemma holds. Then by induction

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m-1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{v}_{1}\in\Std(\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1}\in\Std(>\lambda)\\
\mathsf{u}_{1}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}.

(4.12)

For
\mathsf{v}_{1}\in\Std(\lambda)
, as
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi}
,

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{2}}+\sum_{(\mathsf{u}_{2},\mathsf{v}_{2})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{v}_{1})}c_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}_{2}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is standard}\\
&\hskip 28.45274pt\text{and $d(\mathsf{v}_{2})=d(\mathsf{v}_{1}){\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is reduced},\\
\sum_{(\mathsf{u}_{2},\mathsf{v}_{2})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{v}_{1})}c_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}_{2}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is not standard}\\
&\hskip 28.45274pt\text{or $d(\mathsf{v}_{2})=d(\mathsf{v}_{1}){\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is not reduced}.\end{cases}

where in both cases, we can write

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{v}_{2}\in\Std(\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u}_{2},\mathsf{v}_{2}\in\Std(>\lambda)\\
\mathsf{u}_{2}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}.

(4.13)

For
\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{u}_{2}\in\Std(>\lambda)
,

\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{2}}+\sum_{(\mathsf{u}_{2},\mathsf{v}_{2})\rhd(\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1})}c_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}_{2}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is standard}\\
&\hskip 28.45274pt\text{and $d(\mathsf{v}_{2})=d(\mathsf{v}_{1}){\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is reduced},\\
\sum_{(\mathsf{u}_{2},\mathsf{v}_{2})\rhd(\mathsf{u}_{1},\mathsf{v}_{1})}c_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}},&\text{ if $\mathsf{v}_{2}=\mathsf{v}_{1}{\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is not standard}\\
&\hskip 28.45274pt\text{or $d(\mathsf{v}_{2})=d(\mathsf{v}_{1}){\cdot}s_{r_{m}}$ is not reduced}.\end{cases}

where since
\mathsf{u}_{1}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}
, we can always write

\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{1}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u}_{2},\mathsf{v}_{2}\in\Std(>\lambda)\\
\mathsf{u}_{2}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}_{2}\mathsf{v}_{2}}.

(4.14)

Therefore, substitute (
4.13
) and (
4.14
) back to (
4.12
), we have

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\lambda)\\
\mathsf{u}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},

which completes the proof. ∎

Lemma 4.15
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
r_{1},r_{2},\ldots,r_{m}
are positive integers such that
r_{1},\ldots,r_{m}<n-1
. Then

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

Proof.

Define
\mu=\lambda|_{n-1}
. As
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
,
\mu\in\mathscr{S}_{n-1}^{\Lambda}\cap(\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi})
. Define
i\in I
such that
\mathbf{i}_{\lambda}=\mathbf{i}_{\mu}\vee i
. As
r_{1},r_{2},\ldots,r_{m}<n-1
, we have

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\theta_{i}(e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}),

where

e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}+\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\mu)}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}.

As
\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\mu)}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\in R^{>\mu}_{n}=R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}
, by
subsection 3.1
,
\theta_{i}(\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\mu)}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

For
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\mu)=\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})
and
\mathbf{i}_{\mu}\vee i=\mathbf{i}_{\lambda}
, define
\mathsf{v}
to be the standard
\lambda
-tableau with
\mathsf{v}|_{n-1}=\dot{\mathsf{v}}
. Hence
\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}
. Therefore

\theta_{i}(\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})=\sum_{\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

So

e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{r_{1}}\psi_{r_{2}}\ldots\psi_{r_{m}}=\theta_{i}(\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\mu}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})+\theta_{i}(\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\mu)}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

∎

4.4. Garnir tableaux

In the following subsections we will prove that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
for
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
. Generally, if
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced or
l(d(\mathsf{t})){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced, it is comparatively easy to prove that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. Our main difficulty is to prove that when
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard then
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. In order to prove this we consider different types of
\mathsf{t}
. Among these cases the hardest part is that when
\mathsf{t}
is a special kind of tableaux which is called the Garnir tableau and
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard. In this subsection we will prove that in such case
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

The method of proving the argument in this subsection is first assuming that
\Shape(\mathsf{t})
is a partition of two rows, and using the similar argument we used in the last section to extend the result to general multipartitions. First we give a detailed definition of garnir tableaux.

We introduce a special kind of tableaux, the Garnir tableaux, which was first introduced by Murphy
[
22
]
. Let
(a,b,m)
be a node of
\lambda
such that
(a+1,b,m)
is also a node of
\lambda
. The
(a,b,m)
-Garnir belt
of
\lambda
consists of the nodes
(a,c,m)
for
b\leq c\leq\lambda_{a}^{(m)}
and the nodes
(a+1,g,m)
for
1\leq g\leq b
. For example here is a picture of the
(2,3,2)
-Garnir belt for
\lambda=(3,1|7,6,5,2)
.

\times

\times

\times

\times

\times

\times

\times

The
(a,b,m)
-Garnir tableau
of shape
\lambda
is the unique maximal standard
\lambda
-tableau with respect to the Bruhat order (
\rhd
) among the standard
\lambda
-tableaux which agree with
\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}
outside the
(a,b,m)
-Garnir belt. For example the following is the
(2,3,2)
-Garnir tableau for
\lambda=(3,1|7,6,5,2)
.

\Bigg(\hskip 2.84526pt\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox Suppose
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})
and
\lambda^{(\ell)}=(\lambda_{1}^{(\ell)},\ldots,\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)})
. Let
(a,b,m)=(k-1,\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)},\ell)
and
\mathsf{t}
be the
(a,b,m)
-Garnir tableau. Let the entry in node
(a,b,m)
of
\mathsf{t}
be
r
. Then
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard.

Definition 4.16
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
with
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})
and
\lambda^{(\ell)}=(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k})
. If
k\geq 2
, and
\mathsf{t}
is the
(k-1,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k},\ell)
-Garnir tableau, then we call
\mathsf{t}
the
last Garnir tableau
of shape
\lambda
, and
r=\mathsf{t}(k-1,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k},\ell)
the
last Garnir entry
of
\mathsf{t}
.

\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard.

Because we are going to play around with
\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}
a lot, we introduce more detailed notation for these elements in the next Lemma.

Lemma 4.17
.

Suppose
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})
. Let
\mathsf{t}
be a
(a,b,m)
-Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
and
\lambda^{(m)}=(\lambda_{1}^{(m)},\ldots,\lambda_{k}^{(m)})
. Suppose

\begin{cases}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}(a,b,m)&=l,\\
\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}(a,\lambda_{a}^{(m)},m)&=s,\\
\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}(a+1,b,m)&=t.\end{cases}

Then
l\leq s<t
. Write
t-s=c
,

\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}=\psi_{s}\psi_{s+2}\ldots\psi_{t-1}{\cdot}\psi_{s-1}\psi_{s}\ldots\psi_{t-2}{\cdot}\ldots{\cdot}\psi_{l+1}\psi_{l+2}\ldots\psi_{l+c}{\cdot}\psi_{l}\psi_{l+1}\ldots\psi_{l+c-2}

where

l(\psi_{s}\psi_{s+1}\ldots\psi_{t-1})=l(\psi_{s-1}\psi_{s}\ldots\psi_{t-2})=\ldots=l(\psi_{l+1}\psi_{l+2}\ldots\psi_{l+c})=c

and

l(\psi_{l}\psi_{l+1}\ldots\psi_{l+c-2})=c-1.

Proof.

The Lemma follows by direct calculation. ∎

\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}=\psi_{17}\psi_{18}\psi_{19}{\cdot}\psi_{16}\psi_{17}\psi_{18}{\cdot}\psi_{15}\psi_{16}\psi_{17}{\cdot}\psi_{14}\psi_{15}

with

l(\psi_{17}\psi_{18}\psi_{19})=l(\psi_{16}\psi_{17}\psi_{18})=l(\psi_{15}\psi_{16}\psi_{17})=3=c

and

l(\psi_{14}\psi_{15})=2=c-1.

Remark 4.19
.

For
a\leq b-1
, we will write
\psi_{a,b}=\psi_{a}\psi_{a+1}\psi_{a+2}\ldots\psi_{b-2}\psi_{b-1}
and
\psi_{b,a}=\psi^{*}_{a,b}
in order to simplify our notations.

Our first step is to prove that when
\lambda
is a partition with two rows and
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
with
r
as its last Garnir entry, then
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
for any
\mathsf{s}\in\Std(\lambda)
. We set
\lambda=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})
and without loss of generality, set
\Lambda=\Lambda_{0}
. Therefore
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{n}
with
n=\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2}
. Also we set
\mu=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}-1,1)
,
\dot{\lambda}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2})
and
\dot{\mu}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2}-1,1)
. Furthermore, let
i=\res(\gamma_{1})
,
j=\res(\gamma_{2})
, where
\gamma_{1}=(1,\lambda_{1},1)
and
\gamma_{2}=(2,\lambda_{2},1)
.

First we prove a few useful Lemmas.

Lemma 4.20
.

Suppose
\lambda
,
\dot{\lambda}
,
\dot{\mu}
,
i
and
j
are defined as above, we have

e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}=_{\lambda}\begin{cases}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}y_{n}\\
\hskip 39.83385pt-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}},&\text{ if $i=e-1$, $j\neq e-1$,}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}y_{n}\\
\hskip 39.83385pt-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}\\
\hskip 79.66771pt-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}},&\text{ if $i=j=e-1$,}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}\\
\hskip 39.83385pt+\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\mu}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\mu}},&\text{ if $i=j=e-2$,}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

Proof.

In order to make the notation and diagrams clearer we set
e=4
. For the other choices of
e
one can check that the argument is the same because the proof does not depend on the value of
e
.

Therefore, the Lemma is equivalent to moving all of the dots from the top to the bottom of the diagram. In order to do this we have to consider several cases.

Case
4.4
a:

i\neq e-2,e-1
.

Because we set
e=4
so in this case we have
i\neq 2,3
. As
i\neq 3
,
\delta_{i,3}=0
. Therefore there are no dots on the strand labelled by
i
. And as
i\neq 2
, by relation
2.10
, we have
