\displaystyle\hskip-14.22636pt=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}+\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\mu}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\mu}},

which completes the proof. ∎

Remark 4.21
.

If
\lambda_{1}>\lambda_{2}
and
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of
\lambda
, by
subsection 4.4
we have

\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}\psi_{r}=\psi_{a_{n},n}\psi_{a_{n-1},n-1}\ldots\psi_{a_{r+2},r+2}\psi_{a_{r+1},r+1}.

Define
\mathsf{w}
to be the last Garnir tableau of shape
\dot{\lambda}
, we see that
\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}=\psi_{a_{n-1},n-1}\ldots\psi_{a_{r+2},r+2}\psi_{a_{r+1},r+1}
. Hence
e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}\psi_{r}=\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r})
.

Lemma 4.22
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
and
\dot{\mathsf{t}}
are the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
and
\dot{\lambda}
respectively with last Garnir entry
r
. Set

\psi=\begin{cases}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}y_{n}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1},&\text{ if $i=e-1$, $j\neq e-1$.}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}y_{n}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\lambda_{n-2},&\text{ if $i=j=e-1$.}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

For any standard
\dot{\lambda}
-tableau
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
, if
d(\mathsf{t})\leq m_{\lambda}
and
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}
, then

\begin{cases}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n},&\text{ if $i=j=e-2$,}\\
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

Proof.

If it is not the case that
i=j=e-2
. By
subsection 4.4
we have

\psi{\cdot}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}=_{\lambda}e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda})y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}.

Then we have

\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})=\psi{\cdot}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})},

where as
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}
, then
d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})<d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})
and

l(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})})<l(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1})+l(d(\dot{\mathsf{t}}))=l(d(t))\leq m_{\lambda}.

Then by
subsection 4.2
we have
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

For
i=j=e-2
, set
\dot{\mu}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2}-1,1)
,
\gamma=\lambda|_{n-1}=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}-1)
and
\dot{\gamma}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2}-1)
. Because
y_{\dot{\gamma}}=y_{\dot{\mu}}
. By
subsection 4.4
,

\displaystyle\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}-\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\mu}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}-\theta_{i}(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\gamma}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}-\theta_{i}(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\gamma}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\gamma}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}).

Again by
subsection 4.4
,
\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\gamma}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\gamma}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=_{\gamma}e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}
. Since
\gamma=\lambda|_{n-1}
, by
subsection 3.1
,

\theta_{i}(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\gamma}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\gamma}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})})=_{\lambda}\theta_{i}(e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}).

Therefore

\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})=_{\lambda}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}-\theta_{i}(e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}).

As
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
|\gamma|=n-1<|\lambda|

e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=\sum_{\mathsf{y}\in\Shape(\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\mathsf{y}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}y}+\sum_{\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}\in\Std(>\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}\psi_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}.

(4.23)

For the first term of the left hand side of (
4.23
), because
\gamma=\lambda|_{n-1}
and
j=i=e-2
, we have
b_{i}^{\gamma}=2
. By
subsection 3.1
and the definition of
\gamma
,
\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\mathsf{y}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. For the second term of the left hand side of (
4.23
), as
\mathsf{x},\mathsf{y}\in\Std(>\gamma)=\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})
,
\psi_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}}\in R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}
. By
subsection 3.1
,
\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{x}\mathsf{y}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}\subseteq R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. Therefore,

\theta_{i}(e_{\gamma}y_{\gamma}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

Finally, as

l(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})})<l(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1})+l(d(\dot{\mathsf{t}}))=l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda},

by
subsection 4.2
we have
e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}\subseteq R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. Hence
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. This completes the proof. ∎

Lemma 4.24
.

Suppose
\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}\equiv e-1\pmod{e}
, i.e.
i=j
, and
(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}+1)\lambda_{2}-1\leq m_{\lambda}
. Let
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
and
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
be standard
\lambda|_{n-1}
-tableaux with
\dot{\mathsf{u}}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}
. Assume
i=j\neq e-2
. Then set

\psi=\begin{cases}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}y_{n}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2},&\text{ if $i=j=e-1$,}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1},&\text{ if $i=j\neq e-1,e-2$.}\end{cases}

and we have

\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

Proof.

We assume that
i=j\neq e-2
. First we need to introduce some properties of
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
. Because
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
is a standard
\lambda|_{n-1}
-tableau and
\dot{\mathsf{u}}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}
, the only possible choice of
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
is that
\dot{\mathsf{u}}|_{n-2}=\mathsf{t}^{(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2}-1)}
. Define
\mathsf{u}
and
\mathsf{v}
to be the unique standard
\lambda
-tableau with
\mathsf{u}|_{n-1}=\dot{\mathsf{u}}
and
\mathsf{v}|_{n-1}=\dot{\mathsf{v}}
, respectively. For example, when
\lambda=(7,4)
and
e=3
, then
\dot{\mathsf{u}}=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$6$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$10$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$7$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$8$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$9$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,
and
\mathsf{u}=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$6$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$10$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$7$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$8$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$9$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$11$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,
. From the definitions of
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
,
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
and
\mathsf{u}
,
\mathsf{v}
we see that
d(\mathsf{v})=d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})
and
l(d(\mathsf{u}))=l(d(\dot{\mathsf{u}}))=\lambda_{2}-1
. Notice that if
i=j\neq e-2
, then
\mathbf{i}_{\lambda}=\mathbf{i}_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\vee i
and
y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}=y_{\lambda}
.

Now we consider different cases for
i,j
. Suppose
i=j\neq e-1,e-2
, then

\displaystyle\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\vee i)y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}.

Recall that
e\geq 3
. As
\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}\equiv e-1\pmod{e}
, we must have
\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}\geq e-1\geq 2
. Also because of
\lambda_{2}\geq 1
,

m_{\lambda}\geq(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}+1)\lambda_{2}-1\geq 3\lambda_{2}-1\geq 2\lambda_{2}>l(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})})=2\lambda_{2}-1.

Hence by
subsection 4.2

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{v})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

Suppose
i=j=e-1
, then

\displaystyle\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}y_{n}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\lambda_{n-2})\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\vee i)y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}y_{n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1,n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}-\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}.

As
\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}
doesn’t involve
\psi_{n-1}
, by
subsection 4.2
and
subsection 3.1
,

\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}y_{n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}y_{n}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

As
l(\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1,n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})})=l(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})})=\lambda_{2}-1+\lambda_{2}-1=2\lambda_{2}-2<m_{\lambda}
, by
subsection 4.2
,
\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1,n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}
and
\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}
are both in
R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. Hence
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. ∎

Now we are ready to prove that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
when
\Shape(\mathsf{t})
has only two rows.

Proposition 4.25
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
with
r
to be the last Garnir entry and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Proof.

By
subsection 4.4
, as
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
, we have

\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{\lambda_{1}-1,n-1}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{2},r+1},

where
l(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n})=l(\psi_{\lambda_{1}-1,n-1})=\ldots=l(\psi_{\lambda_{2},r+1})=\lambda_{2}
. We prove the Proposition by induction on
\lambda_{1}
. Recall that we write
\dot{\lambda}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2})
,
\mu=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}-1,1)
and
\dot{\mu}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2}-1,1)
.

When
\lambda_{1}=1
, by definition of Garnir tableau,
\lambda_{1}=\lambda_{2}
. Without loss of generality, we set
\Lambda=\Lambda_{0}
. In this case
i=0
and
j=e-1
. Hence

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}}\psi_{r}=e(0,e-1)\psi_{1}=\psi_{1}e(e-1,0)=0\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

So, when
\lambda_{1}=1
the Proposition is true.

As that the Proposition holds for any partition of two rows with the length of its first row less than
\lambda_{1}
, by
subsection 4.4
we have

\displaystyle\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{t})}\psi_{r}=e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}

(4.26)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\begin{cases}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\lambda}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}+\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\mu}}\vee i)y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}\\
\hskip 39.83385pt=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r})+\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\theta_{i}(e_{\dot{\mu}}y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}),&\text{ if $i=j=e-2$,}\\
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(e_{\dot{\lambda}}y_{\dot{\lambda}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}-1,n-1}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{2}+1,r+2}\psi_{\lambda_{2},r+1})=\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r}),&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

where
\dot{\mathsf{t}}
is the last Garnir tableau with shape
\dot{\lambda}=(\lambda_{1}-1,\lambda_{2})
, and

\psi=\begin{cases}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}y_{n}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1},&\text{ if $i=e-1$, $j\neq e-1$,}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}y_{n}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2},&\text{ if $i=j=e-1$,}\\
\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{2}}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

Now we separate the question into different cases.

Case
4.4
a:

i\neq j
. By (
4.26
) we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r}).

By induction,
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}+\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\dot{\lambda})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}
. Therefore

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})+\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\dot{\lambda})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}).

For
\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\dot{\lambda})
, by
subsection 2.4
,
\res(\dot{\mathsf{u}})=\res(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}})
. Because
i\neq j
, we always have
\Shape(\dot{\mathsf{u}})>\lambda|_{n-1}
. Hence
\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\in R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}
. Therefore by
subsection 3.1
and
subsection 3.1
,
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. So
\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\dot{\lambda})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

For
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})
with
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\unrhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}
, by
subsection 4.4
,
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. Therefore
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. These yield
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Case
4.4
b:

i=j\neq e-2
. By (
4.26
) we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r}).

By induction,
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})\\
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\mathsf{t})\end{subarray}}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}+\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Shape(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}
. Therefore

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})\\
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\mathsf{t})\end{subarray}}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})+\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Shape(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}).

For
\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})
,
\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\in R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}
. As
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
, by
subsection 3.1
we have
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Hence
\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

For
\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})
with
\dot{\mathsf{u}}\rhd\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}
, because
m_{\lambda}\geq d(\mathsf{t})=(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}+1)\lambda_{2}-1
, by
subsection 4.4
we have
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. So
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})\\
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\mathsf{t})\end{subarray}}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

For
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})
with
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}
, by
subsection 4.4
,
\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. So
\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Shape(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi{\cdot}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Therefore we have
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Case
4.4
c:

i=j=e-2
. By (
4.26
) we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r})+\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\theta_{i}(e_{\dot{\mu}}y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}).

(4.27)

For the first term of (
4.27
), by induction,

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})\\
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\dot{\mathsf{t}})\end{subarray}}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})

(4.28)

\displaystyle+\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}).

For
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})
with
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}
, by
subsection 4.4
, we have
\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. Therefore

\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\dot{\lambda})\\
\dot{\mathsf{v}}\rhd\dot{\mathsf{t}}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.29)

For
\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})
with
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\dot{\mathsf{t}})
, by
subsection 2.4
, we have
\res(\dot{\mathsf{u}})=\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\lambda}}
. So the choice of
\dot{\mathsf{u}}
is unique, where
d(\dot{\mathsf{u}})=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}
. Hence as
\mathbf{i}_{\mu}=\mathbf{i}_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\vee i
and
y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}=y_{\mu}

\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{n-1,\lambda_{1}}e(\mathbf{i}_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\vee i)y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{n-1,\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}.

(4.30)

We work with
\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{n-1,\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}=\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{n-2}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}+1}\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}
first. We define a partition
\sigma=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}-2,1)
. Then

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}

(4.31)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-1}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{n-1}\theta_{i-1}(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma})\psi_{n-1}-\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}.

Consider the lefthand term in (
4.31
). As
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
|\sigma|=n-1<|\lambda|
, we have

\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}=\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\text{Std}(\sigma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\sigma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}},

where
\res(\mathsf{u})=\mathbf{i}_{\sigma}{\cdot}s_{\lambda_{1}}s_{\lambda_{1}+1}\ldots s_{n-3}s_{n-2}s_{n-3}\ldots s_{\lambda_{1}+1}s_{\lambda_{1}}=\mathbf{i}_{\sigma}
by
subsection 2.4
, and
\res(\mathsf{v})=\mathbf{i}_{\sigma}
. Since
\text{min}\{\lambda_{1},\ldots,n-2\}=\lambda_{1}
, by
subsection 4.3
,
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}}\neq 0
implies
\mathsf{u}|_{\lambda_{1}-1}\unrhd\mathsf{t}^{\sigma|_{\lambda_{1}-1}}
. Then the unique choice for
\mathsf{u}
is
\mathsf{u}=\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}
. Hence

\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}=c{\cdot}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\sigma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Further more if
\mathsf{u}
is a standard tableau with
\Shape(\mathsf{u})>\sigma
and
\res(\mathsf{u})=\mathbf{i}_{\sigma}
, we must have
\Shape(\mathsf{u})>\lambda|_{n-1}
. Hence by
subsection 3.1
,

\psi_{n-1}\theta_{i-1}(\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\sigma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})\psi_{n-1}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

Therefore

\displaystyle\psi_{n-1}\theta_{i-1}(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma})\psi_{n-1}

\displaystyle=_{\lambda}

\displaystyle c{\cdot}\psi_{n-1}\theta_{i-1}(e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma})\psi_{n-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle c{\cdot}\psi_{n-1}^{2}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}=c{\cdot}(e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}-e_{\mu}y_{\mu}y_{n-1}).

By
subsection 4.2
we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}y_{n-1}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
, we have

\psi_{n-1}\theta_{i-1}(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma})\psi_{n-1}=_{\lambda}c{\cdot}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}.

(4.32)

For the righthand term in (
4.31
), as
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
,
\lambda|_{n-1}\in\mathscr{S}_{n-1}^{\Lambda}\cap(\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi})
. By
subsection 4.3
,

\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\lambda|_{n-1}}y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}=_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}.

Then by
subsection 3.1
,

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{i}(\psi_{\lambda_{1}}\ldots\psi_{n-3}\psi_{n-3}\ldots\psi_{\lambda_{1}}e_{\lambda|_{n-1}}y_{\lambda|_{n-1}})

(4.33)

\displaystyle=_{\lambda}

\displaystyle\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}},

where
\mathsf{u}
is the unique
\mu
-tableau such that
\mathsf{u}|_{n-1}=\dot{\mathsf{u}}
.

So substitute (
4.32
) and (
4.33
) to (
4.31
), we have

\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{n-1,\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\pm c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}}.

As
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
is a standard tableau of shape
\lambda|_{n-1}=\mu|_{n-1}
, we can define
\mathsf{v}_{1}
and
\mathsf{v}_{2}
to be a standard
\mu
-tableau and
\lambda
-tableau where
\mathsf{v}_{1}|_{n-1}=\mathsf{v}_{2}|_{n-1}=\dot{\mathsf{v}}
, respectively. Henceforth
d(\mathsf{v}_{1})=d(\mathsf{v}_{2})=d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})
and by (
4.30
),

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\psi_{n-1,\lambda_{1}}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}\pm c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{d(\mathsf{v}_{1})}\pm c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}}\psi_{d(\mathsf{v}_{2})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\pm c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{2}}\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

Therefore,

\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})\\
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\dot{\mathsf{t}})\end{subarray}}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.34)

Finally, suppose
\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Shape(>\lambda|_{n-1})
, by
subsection 3.1
, we have
\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Therefore

\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

(4.35)

Substitute (
4.29
), (
4.34
) and (
4.35
) to (
4.28
), we have

\psi_{\lambda_{1},n}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.36)

For the second term of (
4.27
), by
subsection 4.4

\displaystyle\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\theta_{i}(e_{\dot{\mu}}y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{i}(\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}e_{\dot{\mu}}y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r})=\theta_{i}(e_{\lambda|_{n-1}}y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r},

where by
subsection 4.3
, because
\psi_{\lambda_{1},n_{1}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}
doesn’t involve
\psi_{n-1}
,

e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{\lambda_{1},n-1}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.37)

Therefore substitute (
4.36
) and (
4.37
) to (
4.27
), we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

Then by
subsection 2.4
the proof is completed. ∎

\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$6$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$7$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$8$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$9$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$10$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,
. Hence

\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}=c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\sigma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

For
\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\sigma)
, we have
\res(\mathsf{u})=\mathbf{i}_{\sigma}=0123012302
. It is impossible that
\Shape(\mathsf{u})=\lambda|_{n-1}
because
\mathbf{i}_{\lambda|_{n-1}}=0123012301
. Hence
\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\sigma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\in R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}
. So
\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma}=c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}}+R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}
and hence by
subsection 3.1
,

\displaystyle\psi_{10}\theta_{1}(\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e_{\sigma}y_{\sigma})\psi_{10}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle c{\cdot}\psi_{10}\theta_{1}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}\mathsf{t}^{\sigma}})\psi_{10}+\psi_{10}\theta_{1}(R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n})\psi_{10}

(4.44)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle c{\cdot}\psi_{10}e(01230123021)y_{4}\psi_{10}+R^{>\lambda}_{n}

\displaystyle=_{\lambda}

\displaystyle c{\cdot}e(01230123012)y_{4}\psi_{10}^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle c{\cdot}e(01230123012)y_{4}y_{10}-c{\cdot}e(01230123012)y_{4}y_{9}

\displaystyle=_{\lambda}

\displaystyle c{\cdot}e(01230123012)y_{4}y_{10}=c{\cdot}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}.

For the right term of (
4.43
), because
\lambda|_{n-1}\in\mathscr{S}_{n-1}^{\Lambda}\cap(\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi})
, by
subsection 4.3
we have

\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e_{\lambda|_{n-1}}y_{\lambda|_{n-1}}=\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}+R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n}.

Then by
subsection 3.1
,

\displaystyle\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e_{\mu}y_{\mu}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{2}(\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e_{\lambda|_{n-1}}y_{\lambda|_{n-1}})

(4.45)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}\theta_{2}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}})+\theta_{2}(R^{>\lambda|_{n-1}}_{n})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\mathsf{t}^{\lambda|_{n-1}}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}+R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

Substitute (
4.44
) and (
4.45
) back to (
4.43
), we have

\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{10}\psi_{9}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e(01230123012)y_{4}=\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{t}^{\mu}}+c{\cdot}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}+R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

Recall
\dot{\mathsf{v}}
is a standard tableau of shape
\lambda|_{n-1}=\mu|_{n-1}
, we can define
\mathsf{v}_{1}\in\Std(\mu)
and
\mathsf{v}_{2}\in\Std(\lambda)
such that
d(\mathsf{v}_{1})=d(\mathsf{v}_{2})=d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})
. Hence by (
4.42
),

\displaystyle\psi_{7,11}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{10}\psi_{9}\psi_{8}\psi_{7}e(0123012301)y_{4}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{v}})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\mathsf{u}\in\Std(\mu)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}_{1}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}_{1}}+c{\cdot}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}_{2}}+R^{>\lambda}_{n}\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n},

which yields

\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(\lambda|_{n-1})\\
(\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}},\dot{\mathsf{t}})\end{subarray}}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{7,11}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.46)

Finally, suppose
\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Shape(>\lambda|_{n-1})
, by
subsection 3.1
we have
\psi_{7,11}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Therefore

\sum_{\dot{\mathsf{u}},\dot{\mathsf{v}}\in\Std(>\lambda|_{n-1})}c_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}}\psi_{7,11}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\dot{\mathsf{u}}\dot{\mathsf{v}}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}.

(4.47)

Substitute (
4.41
), (
4.46
) and (
4.47
) to (
4.40
), we have

\psi_{7,11}\theta_{i}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\dot{\lambda}}\dot{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.48)

For the second term of (
4.39
), by
subsection 4.4

\displaystyle\psi_{7,10}\theta_{i}(e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\mu}})y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{7})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{2}(\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}e(0123013012)y_{4}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{7})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\theta_{2}(e(0123012301)y_{4}\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{7})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle e(01230123012)y_{4}\psi_{7}\psi_{8}\psi_{9}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{7}=e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{7,10}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}.

Then by
subsection 4.3
, because
\psi_{7,10}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}
doesn’t involve
\psi_{10}
, we have
e_{\mu}y_{\mu}\psi_{7,10}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. Therefore

\psi_{7,10}\theta_{i}(e(\mathbf{i}_{\dot{\mu}})y_{\dot{\mu}}\psi_{d(\dot{\mathsf{t}})}\psi_{7})\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}.

(4.49)

Substitute (
4.48
) and (
4.49
) to (
4.39
), we have
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\mu}_{n}
. Finally by
subsection 2.4
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}.

Finally, we can extend the above Proposition to arbitrary multipartition using arguments similar to those we used in the last section.

Corollary 4.50
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
with
r
the last Garnir entry and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
. Therefore, for any standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{s}
,
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{(\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v})\rhd(\mathsf{s},\mathsf{t})}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}
.

Proof.

Write
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})
and
\lambda^{(\ell)}=(\lambda_{1}^{(\ell)},\ldots,\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)})
. If
\lambda^{(\ell)}=\emptyset
, then define
\bar{\lambda}=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)})
. As
l(\bar{\lambda})=\ell-1<l(\lambda)
, we have
\bar{\lambda}\in\mathscr{P}^{\bar{\Lambda}}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\bar{\Lambda}}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\bar{\Lambda}}_{\psi}
. By
subsection 3.3
,
\lambda\in\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{I}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{y}\cap\mathscr{P}^{\Lambda}_{\psi}
, and the Corollary follows.

Now suppose
\lambda^{(\ell)}\neq\emptyset
, First we assume
\mathsf{s}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}
. As
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
,
k\geq 2
. Setting
m=\lambda_{k-1}^{(\ell)}+\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)}
. As
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau, by the definition we see that
\mathsf{t}|_{n-m}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}|_{n-m}
and
k\geq 2
. Define
i
to be the residue of the node
(k-1,1,\ell)
,
\Lambda^{\prime}=\Lambda_{i}
, and
\tilde{\mathsf{t}}
to be the last Garnir tableau of shape
(\lambda_{k-1}^{(\ell)},\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)})
. If we write
\mu=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell-1)},\mu^{(\ell)})
with
\mu^{(\ell)}=(\lambda_{1}^{(\ell)},\ldots,\lambda_{k-2}^{(\ell)})
and
\gamma=(\lambda_{k-1}^{(\ell)},\lambda_{k}^{(\ell)})
, then

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}\hat{\psi}_{r-(n-m)})y_{\mu}.

Recall that
\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}
and
\hat{\psi}_{r-(n-m)}
are elements of
\mathscr{R}_{m}
and
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}
and
\psi_{r-(n-m)}
are elements of
\mathscr{R}_{m}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
. Then by
subsection 4.4
, we have
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r-(n-m)}\in R^{\geq\gamma}_{n}
. Therefore we can write
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r-(n-m)}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}
and hence
\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}\hat{\psi}_{r-(n-m)}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}+r
where
r\in N_{m}^{\Lambda^{\prime}}
. Therefore

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}+\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}+\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(r)y_{\mu}.

For
\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\gamma)
, by
subsection 3.3
we have
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. Hence
\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

For
\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\gamma)
, write
\Shape(\mathsf{u})=\Shape(\mathsf{v})=\sigma
and
\nu=\mu\vee\sigma
. By
subsection 3.3
we have
\nu>\lambda=\mu\vee\gamma
. Then by
subsection 3.3
and
subsection 3.1
,
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\psi_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. Hence
\sum_{\mathsf{u},\mathsf{v}\in\Std(>\gamma)}c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\hat{\psi}_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}})y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
.

Finally by
subsection 3.3
,
\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(r)y_{\mu}\in R^{>\lambda}_{n}
. These yield that

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\hat{\theta}_{\mathbf{i}_{\mu}}(\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\gamma}\tilde{\mathsf{t}}}\psi_{r-(n-m)})y_{\mu}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

Now choose any
\mathsf{s}\in\Std(\lambda)
. Because
\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
, we have

\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}.

Hence

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=\psi^{*}_{d(\mathsf{s})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi^{*}_{d(\mathsf{s})}\psi_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}.

Therefore,
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. By
subsection 2.4
we completes the proof.∎

Remark 4.51
.

Generally it is not easy to find
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}
. Kleshchev-Mathas-Ram
[
14
]
explicitly describes how to compute
c_{\mathsf{u}\mathsf{v}}
where
\Shape(\mathsf{u})=\Shape(\mathsf{v})=\lambda
. This paper also gives an implicit method to compute these coefficients.

4.5. Completion of the
\psi
-problem

In this subsection we are going to prove that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.
subsection 4.2
shows that if
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced then our claim is true. It remains to consider the case when
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced.

First we introduce two special conditions on
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
and
r
for
1\leq r\leq n-1
.

Definition 4.52
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau and
1\leq r\leq n-1
.

(a). If there exists a reduced expression
s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-1}}s_{r_{l}}
of
d(\mathsf{t})
such that
|r-r_{l}|>1
, then
\mathsf{t}
is
unlocked by
s_{r}
in type I
.

(b). If there exists a reduced expression
s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-1}}s_{r_{l}}
of
d(\mathsf{t})
such that
r_{l-1}=r
and
r=r_{l}\pm 1
, then
\mathsf{t}
is
unlocked by
s_{r}
in type II
.

The following Lemmas show that if
l(\mathsf{t})\leq m_{\lambda}
and
\mathsf{t}
is unlocked by
s_{r}
in type I or type II, then we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R_{n}^{\geq\lambda}
.

Lemma 4.53
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
and
\mathsf{s}
are two standard
\lambda
-tableaux with
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{k}
for some
k
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))=l(d(\mathsf{s}))+1
. If for some
r\not\in\{k-1,k,k+1\}
,
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced, then
\mathsf{s}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard, respectively.

Proof.

When
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard, then
r
and
r+1
in
\mathsf{t}
are adjacent, either in the same row or in the same column. Since
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{k}
, we have
\mathsf{s}=\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{k}
. As
r\not\in\{k-1,k,k+1\}
,
r
and
r+1
are in the same nodes in
\mathsf{t}
as in
\mathsf{s}
. Hence
\mathsf{s}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard as well.

When
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced,
d(\mathsf{t})(r)>d(\mathsf{t})(r+1)
. As
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{k}
we have
d(\mathsf{t})(r)=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{k}(r)=d(\mathsf{s})(r)
and
d(\mathsf{t})(r+1)=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{k}(r+1)=d(\mathsf{s})(r+1)
as
r\not\in\{k-1,k,k+1\}
. Hence
d(\mathsf{s})(r)>d(\mathsf{s})(r+1)
. Therefore,
d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced. This completes the proof.∎

Example 4.54
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$7$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$9$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$8$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$6$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$10$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,
and
\mathsf{s}=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$7$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$8$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$9$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$6$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$10$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,
. Then

\displaystyle d(\mathsf{t})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle s_{4}s_{5}s_{6}s_{7}s_{8}s_{6}s_{7}s_{3}s_{4}s_{5}s_{6}s_{4},

\displaystyle d(\mathsf{s})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle s_{7}s_{8}s_{4}s_{5}s_{6}s_{7}s_{3}s_{4}s_{5}s_{6}s_{4}.

Set
k=8
, we have
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{8}
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))=l(d(\mathsf{s}))+1
. Let
r=3
, i.e.
r\not\in\{k-1,k,k+1\}
and
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard. We see that
\mathsf{s}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard either. Similarly, let
r=6
, i.e.
r\not\in\{k-1,k,k+1\}
and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced. Hence
d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced either.

Lemma 4.55
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau with
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
. If
\mathsf{t}
is unlocked by
s_{r}
in type I, then
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
for any standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{s}
.

Proof.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced, by
subsection 4.2
,
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced. Since
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau unlocked by
s_{r}
in type I, by
subsection 4.5
, there exists a reduced expression
s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l}}
of
d(\mathsf{t})
such that
|r-r_{l}|>1
. Define
\mathsf{w}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-1}}
. By
subsection 2.3
,
\mathsf{w}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau. It is easy to see that
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r_{l}}
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))=l(d(\mathsf{w}))+1
. Hence by
subsection 4.5
,
\mathsf{w}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced. So
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}
because
l(d(\mathsf{w}))=l(d(\mathsf{t}))-1<w_{\lambda}
.

We can write
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r_{l}}
as a reduced expression. By
subsection 4.2
, we have

\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}=_{\lambda}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}-\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}\psi_{r_{l}}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}-\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r_{l}}.

Because
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}
and
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
, we have
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. We can write
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r_{l}}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r_{l}}
. Because
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}
, we have
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{w}))<m_{\lambda}
, which yields that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r_{l}}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. Therefore we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
. ∎

Lemma 4.56
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau and that there exists a standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{w}
such that
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r+1}
for some
r
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))=l(d(\mathsf{w}))+2
. If
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced, then
\mathsf{w}{\cdot}s_{r+1}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r+1}
is not reduced, respectively.

Similarly suppose
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r-1}
for some
r
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))=l(d(\mathsf{w}))+2
. If
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced, then
\mathsf{w}{\cdot}s_{r-1}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r-1}
is not reduced, respectively.

Proof.

Suppose
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r+1}
. If
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard,
r
and
r+1
are adjacent in
\mathsf{t}
. But
r
and
r+1
occupy the same positions as
r+1
and
r+2
, respectively in
\mathsf{w}
. So
\mathsf{w}{\cdot}s_{r+1}
is not standard. If
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced, as
d(\mathsf{w})^{-1}(r+1)=d(\mathsf{t})^{-1}(r)
and
d(\mathsf{w})^{-1}(r+2)=d(\mathsf{t})^{-1}(r+1)
, by
subsection 2.2
, then
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced implies
d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r+1}
is not reduced. The other case is similar.

Remark 4.57
.

In
subsection 4.5
and
subsection 4.5
, when we say
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}
or
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r+1}
, it means
d(\mathsf{t})
and
d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}
or
d(\mathsf{t})
and
d(\mathsf{s}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r+1}
are the same as permutations.

, we have

Lemma 4.59
.

Suppose
\lambda\in\mathscr{S}_{n}^{\Lambda}
and
\mathsf{t}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau with
l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
. If
\mathsf{t}
is unlocked by
s_{r}
in type II, then
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
for any standard
\lambda
-tableau
\mathsf{s}
.

Proof.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is standard and
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is reduced. Then, by
subsection 4.2
,
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{t}){\cdot}s_{r}
is not reduced. Then, by
subsection 4.5
, there exists a reduced expression
s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-1}}s_{r_{l}}
for
d(\mathsf{t})
such that
r_{l-1}=r
and
r=r_{l}\pm 1
. Without loss of generality, set
r=r_{l}-1
. Define
\mathsf{w}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}s_{r_{1}}s_{r_{2}}\ldots s_{r_{l-2}}
. By
subsection 2.3
,
\mathsf{w}
is a standard
\lambda
-tableau. It is easy to see that
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r+1}
and
l(d(\mathsf{t}))=l(d(\mathsf{w}))+2
. Hence, by
subsection 4.5
,
\mathsf{w}{\cdot}s_{r+1}
is not standard or
d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r+1}
is not reduced. So
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r+1}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}
because
l(d(\mathsf{w}))=l(d(\mathsf{t}))-2<w_{\lambda}
.

Because
d(\mathsf{t})=d(\mathsf{w}){\cdot}s_{r}s_{r+1}
as a reduced expression, by
subsection 4.2
, we have

\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}=_{\lambda}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}-\psi_{d(\mathsf{s})}^{*}e_{\lambda}y_{\lambda}\psi_{d(\mathsf{w})}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}=\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}-\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}.

(4.60)

Now
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}
, so
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{t}))\leq m_{\lambda}
. Hence we have

\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{t}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}.

(4.61)

Let
\res(\mathsf{w})=i_{1}i_{2}\ldots i_{n}
be the residue sequence of
\mathsf{w}
. Then

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}=\begin{cases}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}\pm\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}},&\text{ if $i_{r}=i_{r+2}=i_{r+1}\pm 1$,}\\
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1},&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

Because
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r+1}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathsf{v}\in\Std(\lambda)\\
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}\end{subarray}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}
,

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}=_{\lambda}\sum_{\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}}c_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}.

Since
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}
,
l(d(\mathsf{v}))<l(d(\mathsf{w}))=l(d(\mathsf{t}))-2\leq m_{\lambda}-2
. Hence,
l(\psi_{d(\mathsf{v})}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1})=l(d(\mathsf{v}))+2<m_{\lambda}
. By
subsection 4.2
we have
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{v}}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
if
\mathsf{v}\rhd\mathsf{w}
. Therefore, we always have

\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{w}}\psi_{r+1}\psi_{r}\psi_{r+1}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}

(4.62)

in both cases. Substituting (
4.61
) and (
4.62
) into (
4.60
) shows that
\psi_{\mathsf{s}\mathsf{t}}\psi_{r}\in R^{\geq\lambda}_{n}
.∎

The following Lemmas are technical results which we will use later.

Lemma 4.63
.

Suppose
\mathsf{t}\in\Std(\lambda)
with
d(\mathsf{t})=s_{n-1}s_{n-2}\ldots s_{r+1}
, and
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard. Then
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau of shape
\lambda
.

Proof.

As
d(\mathsf{t})
is the standard expression, we have
w_{n}=s_{n-1}
,
w_{n-1}=s_{n-2},\ldots,w_{r+2}=s_{r+1}
and
\mathsf{t}=\mathsf{t}^{(1)}=\mathsf{t}^{(2)}=\ldots=\mathsf{t}^{(r+1)}
. Write
\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)})
and
\lambda^{(\ell)}=(\lambda^{(\ell)}_{1},\ldots,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k})
, as
\mathsf{t}^{(n)}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}w_{n}=\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}{\cdot}s_{n-1}
is standard,
n-1
and
n
are not adjacent in
\mathsf{t}^{\lambda}
. This forces
\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k}=1
.

By (
2.29
) we have

\mathsf{t}^{-1}(k)=\begin{cases}(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda})^{-1}(k-1),&\text{ if $r+2\leq k\leq n$,}\\
(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda})^{-1}(n),&\text{ if $k=r+1$,}\\
(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda})^{-1}(k),&\text{ otherwise.}\end{cases}

and since
\mathsf{t}{\cdot}s_{r}
is not standard,
r
and
r+1
are adjacent in
\mathsf{t}
. As
\mathsf{t}^{-1}(r+1)=(\mathsf{t}^{\lambda})^{-1}(n)=(k,\lambda^{(\ell)}_{k},\ell)=(k,1,\ell)
, we must have
\mathsf{t}^{-1}(r)=(k-1,1,\ell)
. This shows that
\mathsf{t}
is the last Garnir tableau with shape
\lambda
.∎

Example 4.64
.

Suppose
\lambda=(4,4,1)
and
\mathsf{t}=\mbox{\tiny$\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\vbox{\vbox{\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$1$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$2$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$3$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$4$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$5$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$7$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$8$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$9$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt\moveright 0.0pt\vbox{\hrule height=0.3pt\hbox{\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt\hbox to5.4381pt{\hfil$6$\hfil}\vrule height=4.35048pt,width=0.3pt,depth=1.0876pt}\hrule height=0.3pt}\vskip-0.3pt}}\hskip 0.0pt$}\,

d(\mathsf{t})=s_{8}s_{7}s_{6}
